title: “Have you played Atari today?”
lede: At its peak Atari was the largest advertiser in its industry. These are spots from the boom, a local news report filed as the company came apart, the 2014 excavation and the last console to carry the name before it was sold.

videos.title: Atari Video Computer System commercial
videos.caption: An early spot for the cartridge console. The 1978 date is the uploader’s. A reference history says Atari spent $6 million on advertising in the last seven weeks of 1978 to clear unsold stock.[^25]

videos.title: Pac-Man for the Atari 2600
videos.caption: The home version was “widely faulted for the quality of its graphic display” and still sold well.[^1] The 1982 date is the uploader’s.

videos.title: Berzerk: “Have you played Atari today?”
videos.caption: A cartridge spot that closes on the company’s jingle. Atari spent $28.5 million on television in the first nine months of 1982.[^8] The year is the uploader’s.

videos.title: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial for the Atari 2600
videos.caption: The Christmas 1982 spot for one of the film-licensed games that were not “the blockbusters Atari expected.”[^1] Copies were found in the Alamogordo landfill in 2014.[^22] The year is the uploader’s.

videos.title: CBS 8 San Diego special report on the video game slump
videos.caption: A ten-minute local news report from the station’s own archive, dated 1984 by the station, on the collapse of the home video game business.

videos.title: KRQE: cartridges found at the Atari dig
videos.caption: Albuquerque television on the April 26, 2014 excavation of the Alamogordo landfill, which confirmed the 1983 burial.[^22][^4]

videos.title: Atari Jaguar: “Do the Math”
videos.caption: Atari Corporation’s 64-bit console sold about 125,000 units from late 1993 to the end of 1995.[^11] The 1994 date is the uploader’s.

note: Air dates marked as the uploader’s could not be confirmed independently.
